newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS FACE PROMOTED LECCE IN SERIE A OPENER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS FACE PROMOTED LECCE IN SERIE A OPENER.

text.p: Newly-promoted Lecce and Brescia face a daunting start to their serie A season on August 31.
The fixtures list published on Thursday paired Lecce with Italian champions Juventus, while Brescia face Internazionale -- both away.
The first major league clash does not come until September 14, when Rome club Lazio, tipped to do well with Croat striker Alen Boksic back in attack, visit AC Milan.
Fans have to wait until December for the first encounter between title favourites Juventus and Inter.
Much is expected of Inter after they signed Ronaldo from Barcelona and midfielder Diego Simeone from Atletico Madrid. Transfer talks involving Ronalso are deadlocked at present.
African Footballer of the Year Nwankwo Kanu of Nigeria, who failed to play for Inter after signing last season, is also back after a heart operation.
Juventus have sold striker Christian Vieri to Atletico Madrid and Boksic but have strengthened their attack by buying Filippo Inzaghi, serie A's top scorer last season with Atalanta.
He will partner Italy international Alessandro Del Piero up front.
Otherwise Juventus coach Marcello Lippi, who took the Turin side to its 24th championship last season, has left the squad largely unchanged.
Lippi said at the weekend the main challenge to Juventus this year would come from the two Milan teams, last season's runners-up Parma, and Lazio.
AC Milan suffered one of their worst league runs in 1996-97, finishing 11th, and have brought back coach Fabio Capello to knock them into shape.
Capello led Milan to four league championships between 1991 and 1996 but left Italy to help Real Madrid to the Spanish crown last season.

Milan have signed striker Patrick Kluivert from Ajax Amsterdam and French midfielder Ibrahim Ba from Bordeaux. The team start their league campaign away to Piacenza and do not meet Juventus until November.
Roma, who also spent heavily, and Sampdoria, with newly-signed German striker Juergen Klinsmann, are seen as other title outsiders.
Italian soccer federation president Luciano Nizzola said that all matches will be monitored by television to help spot violent play.
